summary: Backend smoke + feature testing for multi-customer inventory system. 31/33 backend checks passed. Two CSV export endpoints return 500 due to non-ASCII Turkish characters in Content-Disposition filename header (UnicodeEncodeError: 'latin-1' codec can't encode character '\u015f').
passed: GET /api/auth/me with Bearer token returns admin
GET /api/customers returns 6 seeded Müşteri A..F with valid UUID ids
POST /api/customers/{id}/products creates product; initial movement logged when qty>0
Product isolation: A's product not visible in B's list
Order preview: per_package, required, available, sufficient, insufficient[] correct
Order create with sufficient stock: deducts qty, creates order, logs movement kind='order' with negative delta
Order insufficient stock -> 400 Turkish message 'Yetersiz stok...' AND no deduction occurs
STOCK ISOLATION verified: order for A does not affect B's identically-named product qty
GET /api/dashboard/summary: total_customers=6, per_customer len=6, recent sorted desc, low_stock array present
DELETE product and DELETE package work

failed.issue: HTTP 500 UnicodeEncodeError: 'latin-1' codec can't encode character '\u015f' (ş) in Content-Disposition filename. csv_response builds filename as f'stok_{c[name]}.csv' where c['name']='Müşteri A' -> Starlette rejects non-latin-1 header value.
failed.evidence: server.py:448 StreamingResponse headers={'Content-Disposition': f'attachment; filename="stok_Müşteri A.csv"'}; traceback in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log

failed.issue: Same UnicodeEncodeError as products export (filename contains 'Müşteri').

action_items: Fix csv_response in /app/backend/server.py to encode filename using RFC 5987. Example: from urllib.parse import quote; ascii_name = c['name'].encode('ascii','ignore').decode() or 'export'; disposition = f"attachment; filename=\"{ascii_name}.csv\"; filename*=UTF-8''{quote(f'{prefix}_{c[name]}.csv')}". Or simply slugify/transliterate Turkish chars (ş->s, ü->u, ö->o, ç->c, ğ->g, ı->i) before putting into filename.

After fix, re-run export endpoints — they should return 200 with body starting with BOM (\ufeff) and headers 'name,sku,unit,quantity,low_stock_threshold' for products and movement headers for movements.
